notes: Degenerate comparison this iteration: the baseline points at skill-snapshot/, which is a byte copy of the live skill (no edits were made), so both configs ran identical instructions. The +0.11 pass-rate delta, +9.4s time, and token delta are run-to-run variance, not a skill effect. This iteration establishes a reference point for future edited iterations, not a skill-vs-no-skill lift.

Only one run per configuration exists, so the reported 0% stddev is not informative (runs_per_configuration says 3 by default). Any real variance is unmeasured; expectation 4 flipping between the two runs is itself evidence of nonzero variance.

The single discriminating assertion is expectation 4: the with_skill run's fix deleted the author's pivot/landing line 「但我能确定的是，你还在听我念叨」 along with the trailing named-emotion, instead of preserving it as the last line. The baseline run kept it. This is the actionable signal — the skill's Part 4.4 'delete the conclusion' guidance can over-delete and take the good perception line with it. Candidate skill improvement: make 4.4 stress landing ON the buried perception, not merely cutting the tail.

The other 8 assertions passed identically in both runs (stop-at-first-failure, no scorecard, correct 4.2/S.1 diagnosis, no false 4.1 charge on the pivot, newsletter-aware, no R warning, specific positive, no sympathy-fishing rewrite) — non-discriminating here, but they guard against regressions worth keeping.

Token magnitudes in the summary reflect output_chars (grading.json's timing block pre-empted timing.json's total_tokens in the aggregator), not true LLM tokens; the real executor cost was ~31k tokens per run. Time figures are accurate.
